course_description:
Conceptual framework of field of auditing. Problem-solving skills to carry out effective and efficient audits.

The course focus on developing auditing and analytical skills. Students develop practical skills in audit planning, evaluating an audit client’s organisational systems, performing audit testing, and preparing audit reports. Case studies are used extensively to build experience in solving real-world audit problems. The analytical and professional judgement skills developed in this course are highly valuable for students’ future careers.

course_aims: This course aims to provide a comprehensive and integrated introduction to the environment and methodology of auditing. It is intended to provide the theoretical framework around which auditing knowledge and skills can be built by further study or on the job experience.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the nature and functions of auditing in the context of the audit engagement/different types of audits.
Analyse the ethical and legal issues faced by auditors to form professional judgements on the appropriate course of action.

Apply the stages of audit planning and preliminary procedures to form an understanding of the audit client and its environment in order to develop audit strategies and design appropriate audit procedures.

Assess the audit client's risks, including carrying out an evaluation of the client's internal control system, and design appropriate audit procedures to test for material misstatements in financial statements.
Design audit procedures to complete the audit (including detecting subsequent events) and use professional judgement to form an audit opinion.
Work on audit issues as a member of a team.

assessment_details.task_description: Group Case Study Overview This group case study provides you with practical experience in audit planning, identifying risks, conducting tests of control procedures, and performing substantive testing. The analytical skills are highly valuable to your future career, regardless of your career choices. The case study has a word limit of 1200 words. Each group should consist of 2 members. Students struggling to find another student to work with should contact the Course Coordinator. Further instructions are available on the Course Blackboard site. Case Study Instructions The case study consists of performing several tasks and completing the working papers provided. Follow these guidelines when preparing and submitting your work: Register your case study group using the case study group signup link in the case study assessment folder on Blackboard one week before the case study is due. Save your case study as a Word document. PDF submissions will not be accepted. Upload the completed case study to Blackboard via Turn-it-in before the deadline. After submitting the case study, perform peer assessment via Buddy Check in the case study assessment folder on Blackboard. Important Submission Details Include names of both group members in your submission. Avoid last-minute submissions, as system issues can arise due to high traffic. Late submissions without an approved extension will be penalised according to university policy. After submission, take a screenshot of your receipt as proof. Retain this receipt for your records. For detailed information on the case study's format, expectations, and submission, please refer to the notice in the "Assignment" folder on Blackboard. learning_activities.topic: Topic 1 Introduction & Audit objectives In Week 1, we will discuss what an audit is about, different types of audits and auditors, and the various audit objectives. Relevant readings: Arens (Chapters 1 and 4). Learning outcomes: L01
Workshop 1: Introduction & Audit objectives Learning outcomes: L01

Topic 2: Audit risk model & Audit evidence In Topic 2, we will introduce various ways auditors collect audit evidence and we will also briefly discuss the various components of the audit risk model. Relevant reading: Arens (Chapters 5 and 7 (p.232-236)) Learning outcomes: L03, L04

Workshop 2: Audit risk model & Audit evidence Public holiday: EKKA day is on 12 August 2026. Our Wednesday workshop on 12 August will be rescheduled to another day of the week and this will be reflected in your personalised timetable. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Topic 3: Audit planning, materiality and risk In Topic 3, we continue to learn how audit risk model works. In particular, we will learn how audit risks and inherent risks are assessed. In addition, we explore how materiality thresholds are set at the planning stage and subsequently how they are used to identify material misstatements. Relevant reading: Arens (Chapters 6 and 7) Public holiday: EKKA day is on 12 August 2026. Our Wednesday lecture on 12 August will be rescheduled to another day of the week and this will be reflected in your personalised timetable. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06
Workshop 3: Audit planning, materiality and risk Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Topic 4: Internal control, control risk and fraud On Topic 4, we will discuss the types of internal controls implemented by reporting entities that contributing to higher quality financial information, how control risks are assessed and tested by auditors. Relevant reading: Arens (Chapters 8 and 9) Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06
Workshop 4: Internal control, control risk and fraud Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Topic 5: Tests of controls and substantive tests 1 On Topic 5, we introduce the concept of tests of controls and substantive testing, and how these concepts, along with other concepts we have learned so far, are applied in sales and collection cycle. Relevant reading: Arens (Chapters 11, 12 and 13). Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06
Workshop 5: Tests of controls and substantive tests 1 Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Topic 6: Audit sampling On Topic 6, we explore how sampling techniques are applied in audit testing with practical examples. Relevant readings: Gay and Simnett (Chapter 10) Learning outcomes: L04, L06
Workshop 6: Audit Sampling Learning outcomes: L04, L06

Topic 7: Tests of controls and substantive tests 2 On Topic 7, we will explore how tests of controls and substantive tests are applied in the audit of 1) cash and PPE accounts and 2) the following transactions cycles: inventory and warehousing and payroll and personnel. Relevant reading: Arens (Chapters 15 and 16) Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06
Workshop 7: Tests of controls and substantive tests 2 Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Topic 8: Tests of controls and substantive tests 3 On Topic 8, we will identify tests of controls and substantive testing relevant for the acquisition and payment cycle and capital acquisition and repayment cycle. We will also briefly discuss how auditors could sensibly use the work of others (ISAs 600-620). Relevant Reading: Arens (Chapters 15 and 16) Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06
Workshop 8: Tests of controls and substantive tests 3 Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Topic 9: Completing the audit On Topic 9, we identify audit procedures to complete the audit process, including identifying and assessing subsequent events and contingent liabilities. We will also briefly discuss the sustainability assurance standards (ISSA/ASSA 5000 series). Additionally, we will also briefly discuss the scope and the key characteristics of ISSA/ASSA differ from the ISAE 3000 (Revised) Assurance Engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information). Relevant Reading: Arens (Chapter 17). Learning outcomes: L05, L06
In-Semester Break
Workshop 9: Completing the audit Learning outcomes: L05, L06

Topic 10 Audit reports In Topic 10, we will demonstrate what the end product of the audit processes - an audit report - looks like, and conditions under which each type of audit report are issued. We will also discuss the key elements of the audit quality management and engagement quality reviews (ISQM/ASQM 1, ISA/ASA 220 and ISQM/ASQM 2). Relevant reading: Arens (Chapter 18) Learning outcomes: L01, L05
Workshop 10: Audit reports Learning outcomes: L01, L05

Topic 11 Ethics, Auditor legal liabilities In Topic 11, we explore ethical requirements auditors need to follow. More importantly, what legal consequences auditors could be facing if they failed to provide quality services to their clients. Relevant reading: Gay and Simnett (Chapter 2 and 3). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06
Workshop 11: Ethics, Auditor legal liabilities Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06
Revision lecture We will provide some information on the final exam and go through some mock final exam papers. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Workshop 12: Drop-in Sessions Students who are interested in some contemporary audit issues or wish to trouble shooting some problems will be provided additional assistance in this session. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
